title: Round-number stop cascade: buy the first 15m close through a fresh round level, target the next level
ex_ante_rule: Chart: closed 15m candles only; every signal is evaluated at bar close and filled at the next bar's open. Long only, spot, one position, whole allowed balance, no pyramiding. ROUND GRID: once per UTC day, take P = close of the last 15m bar of the previous UTC day (the 23:45 bar). Step S = the largest number of the form 1, 2.5 or 5 times a power of ten (..., 1, 2.5, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100, 250, 500, 1000, ...) that is <= 0.02*P (e.g. BTC 60000 -> 1000, ETH 3000 -> 50, BNB 600 -> 10). S stays fixed for the whole UTC day. Levels are integer multiples of S. ENTRY at the close of bar t when ALL hold: (1) L = floor(close(t)/S)*S, the highest level at or below close(t), and close(t-1) < L (so close(t-1) < L <= close(t); if a bar crosses several levels, L is the highest one crossed); (2) close(t) >= 1.002*L; (3) the level is fresh: the highest high of the 32 bars t-32..t-1 (8 hours, excluding bar t) is < L; (4) close(t) > SMA(96) of 15m closes (24-hour mean, including bar t); (5) no position is open; (6) no earlier entry at the same level L on the same UTC day. Record L and S at signal time; they do not change during the trade. EXIT, whichever comes first: (a) TAKE-PROFIT: limit at L + S (the next round level up), filled intrabar as soon as high >= L + S (at the open if the bar opens above it); (b) STOP: at L - 0.5*S, fixed at entry, triggered intrabar as soon as low touches it (implemented as a custom stop fixed at entry, i.e. a fixed per-trade percentage (fill - (L - 0.5*S))/fill below the fill price; plus a native backstop stoploss of 3% below entry, which the structural stop should always precede); (c) TIME EXIT: market exit at the open of the bar 32 bars (8 hours) after the entry bar (signal at the close of the 32nd bar held, fill at the next open). Every trade closes within 8 hours, well under 24 hours. No cooldown other than condition (6). No other filters. Warm-up: 400 bars (longest lookback SMA(96) plus up to 192 bars to obtain the previous UTC day's last close, rounded up generously).
rationale: Osler (FRBNY SR125) found in a dealer's order book that stop-loss buy orders cluster just above round numbers, and SR150 shows that executed stop orders feed self-reinforcing price cascades. Shorts (and in crypto, perp shorts whose liquidation prices sit at the same psychologically placed levels) who put stops just above an untested round price are forced to buy at market when it breaks; that forced, price-insensitive buying is the counterparty that gives the move away. The first clean close through a level untouched for 8 hours, in a market above its 24h mean, is when the most resting stops are still there. The target is the next round level, S away; by grid construction S is 0.8-2% of price, so after the 0.2% confirmation the gross aim is about 0.6-1.8% (typically ~1%), above the 0.30% base and 0.45% conservative round trip; the stop is half a step (~0.4-1.0% below entry), so a loss costs less than a win gains. Expected frequency: a 1-2% grid crossed upward through a fresh level with price above the 24h mean happens several times a week per pair; I expect roughly 150-350 trades per year per pair, inside the owner's 150-500 target. The 8-hour time exit and the half-step stop cap any one loss near 1% plus cost, so long losing streaks (the H-005 failure) cannot reach the 25% drawdown ceiling quickly. Success criteria: the existing gates (positive net at base and conservative cost, drawdown < 25% at optimistic/base/conservative, >= 30 trades per split, same rule on all three pairs). No backtest of this rule has been seen; all numbers are those of the idea, fixed in advance.
novelty_vs_tried: No tried family uses absolute price levels. Every earlier breakout (Donchian, weekly breakout, squeeze, inside bar, opening range, swing structure) defines the level from recent highs/lows or volatility of the series itself; here the level is an exogenous round number on a price-proportional 1/2.5/5 grid, where order-book studies place stop clusters. The exit is also different: a fixed take-profit at the next round level and a structural stop at half a grid step, with an 8-hour time exit, instead of channel or moving-average exits. It is not a dip-buy and not a slow trend rule.
